title: Mitigate session-index drift causing progressive memory fragmentation and cross-environment OOMs
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments reported gradual GPU OOMs that followed long-running conversational sessions. Investigation shows sessions with repeated mid-length context shifts trigger an interaction between the KV cache index snapshotting and the slab allocator leading to uneven free-list fragmentation. Over time this manifests as small unusable free islands, degraded allocator performance, and eventual OOM on high-util nodes.

Impact: Production incidents affecting 3 enterprise customers (two on Dedicated, one on Private) with sustained degradation for >6 hours in some clusters. Host metrics: GPU memory pressure rising steadily over 12–36 hours, allocator stalls, and increased latency. Customer-facing effects: failed responses, elevated retries, and degraded SLOs.

Root cause hypothesis: A race during session index compaction allows tombstoned index entries to be retained in the slab metadata without being reclaimed. The retained metadata prevents coalescing of nearby free spans, leading to fragmentation under non-uniform allocation patterns (mixed short prefix cache and large KV blobs). The compaction race is exacerbated by continuous background snapshotting on Dedicated and Private where snapshot frequency is high.

Immediate mitigation (hotfix): 1) Backport a conservative GC trigger that forces immediate index reconciliation when slab fragmentation exceeds threshold. 2) Introduce a short-lived allocator fallback that favors best-fit coalescing on affected nodes. 3) Apply per-tenant session TTL enforcement to prevent unbounded long-running sessions while root fix lands. These were deployed to the three affected customers as a staged rollout this week.

Patch details: The runtime patch (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6242) adds: - synchronized index compaction with a lock-free confirmation step to ensure tombstones are eligible for reclamation before metadata release; - a fast-path coalescer that runs opportunistically during KV eviction; - telemetry hooks to emit fragmentation histograms (per-slab, per-tenant) and a new metric runtime.fragmentation_ratio.

Testing and validation: We reproduced the leak locally with a session-replay harness (convo-replay v2) and a synthetic allocator stress test (scripts/prod-sim/frag-sim.sh). Benchmarks show the fix reduces fragmentation_ratio by 78% under the reproducer and eliminates the slow memory creep over a 48h stress run. Added unit tests and an integration stress test to the CI job runtime-stress/frag-regen.

Rollout plan: Canary on hosted infra (10% of traffic) -> Dedicated internal staging -> target customers in Private (one at a time) -> full fleet. Monitor runtime.fragmentation_ratio, GPU memory utilization, and error rate. If fragmentation reduction <60% in canary, roll back and switch to emergency mitigation.

Next steps: 1) Merge runtime-1.20 branch and schedule canary 2026-03-15. 2) Create migration job to run index compact on on-prem clusters older than runtime-1.16. 3) Add eviction policy tweak in Optimize to recommend TTLs for long sessions. 4) Postmortem writeup and customer RCA notes for impacted accounts.

Customer comms: We created private incident threads with the three customers and issued interim remediation notes. Draft PR to formalize SLA credit proposal for impacted windows is in docs/incidents/sla-credit-draft.md.
